body:
WHAT
`REASONING_EFFORTS` is the ordered list of thinking-depth levels a connection can choose: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. The protocol package (the shared TypeScript types the engine and host use) defines it; the app repeats it because it cannot import the engine.

WHY
The order carries meaning — clamping picks the nearest level — so a reordered copy clamps to the wrong one, and a missing level would be refused by the app while the engine accepts it.

WHERE
engine/protocol/src/types.ts — `export const REASONING_EFFORTS` and `type ReasoningEffort`; app/main/config.js — `const REASONING_EFFORTS` (exported). Consumer of the order: engine/providers/src/effort.ts `WIRE_EFFORTS`, `toWireEffort()`, `EffortClamp`.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Deep-equal the two arrays: same length 7, same strings, same order.
2. Assert the first entry is 'off' and the last is 'max' on both sides.
3. Assert WIRE_EFFORTS in effort.ts maps 1:1 onto REASONING_EFFORTS by index with only 'off'→'none' differing (toWireEffort(REASONING_EFFORTS[i]) === WIRE_EFFORTS[i]).
4. Assert no duplicates in either list (new Set(list).size === 7).
